$comment: Declarative source of truth for scripts-utilities. Consumed by modules/*.ps1 (via lib/catalog.ps1), scripts/install-machine-scope.ps1, and (later) the uninstaller and GUI. Stage-1 toolbox contents live in scripts/build-devtoolbox.ps1 and are represented here only as coarse layer toggles. Keep machine_scope_ids in sync with the machineScope entries in build-devtoolbox.ps1.

tools.name: gh
tools.notes: GitHub CLI - auth, PRs, issues, releases

tools.name: pwsh
tools.notes: PowerShell 7 side by side with Windows PowerShell 5.1; installer_type=wix is REQUIRED - winget 7.6.0+ defaults this id to the MSIX, which is single-user, sandboxes $PSHOME and cannot set machine-wide execution policy. CI runners use the MSI, so the MSI is what reproduces them. The wix installer is machine-scope only: --installer-type wix --scope user returns 0x8A150010.

tools.name: fzf
tools.notes: fuzzy finder for interactive CLI selection

tools.name: bat
tools.notes: syntax-highlighted file pager

tools.name: git-delta
tools.notes: syntax-highlighted diff viewer; set as git core.pager

tools.name: just
tools.notes: task runner (Justfile); cross-platform parity with Linux just

tools.name: hyperfine
tools.notes: benchmark runner and CLI timer

tools.name: sops
tools.notes: encrypted YAML/JSON/env secrets management; pairs with age

tools.name: age
tools.notes: modern file encryption; age-keygen generates recipient keys

tools.name: tokei
tools.notes: code statistics and LOC counter

tools.name: podman
tools.notes: daemonless OCI container engine. winget-default is deliberate: the Podman.CLI manifest declares no scope, so BOTH --scope user and --scope machine fail with 0x8A150010 'No applicable installer found' (verified as user and as SYSTEM). With no --scope flag it installs per-user to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Podman and adds itself to the USER PATH - no elevation, no system PATH entry. Linux containers need a VM: `podman machine init --provider hyperv` (Hyper-V feature + Hyper-V Administrators membership, admin for the first init only) or the default WSL provider. Pair with docker-compose for full compose-spec fidelity.

tools.name: docker-compose
tools.notes: standalone Compose v2 binary. Drives Podman over its Docker-compatible API pipe (npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine) - preferred over podman-compose because it is the reference Compose implementation (profiles, ${VAR:-default}, depends_on, project name all behave identically).

tools.name: curl-libressl
tools.notes: curl built against LibreSSL instead of Schannel. Windows' bundled C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe uses Schannel, whose AcquireCredentialsHandle fails with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS inside sandboxed agent runners (see docs/agent-rules.md 'Native HTTPS in agent sandboxes'). This build does TLS in userspace and ships its own curl-ca-bundle.crt, so it works there. Detection uses trurl because System32 curl.exe wins bare-name PATH resolution and would mask a missing install; call this curl.exe by absolute path from its package bin dir.

tools.name: yt-dlp
tools.notes: video/audio downloader (actively maintained youtube-dl fork; supports 1000+ sites). Auto-discovers the toolbox's ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH, so stream-merging (-f bestvideo+bestaudio), audio extraction (-x --audio-format mp3), and remuxing work with no separate ffmpeg install. YouTube needs a JavaScript runtime to solve nsig/PO-token challenges (extraction fails otherwise): the EJS solver SCRIPTS are already bundled in this PyInstaller standalone binary, but the RUNTIME is not - install `deno` (its own catalog entry) and yt-dlp auto-detects it. Refresh the bundled solver between releases with `--remote-components ejs:github`. Self-updates via `yt-dlp -U`, but winget owns this copy - prefer `winget upgrade yt-dlp.yt-dlp` to stay channel-clean.

tools.name: deno
tools.notes: secure JavaScript/TypeScript runtime. Also serves as yt-dlp's JS challenge runtime: yt-dlp enables deno by DEFAULT, auto-detects it on PATH, and runs its bundled EJS scripts under Deno's restricted permissions to solve YouTube nsig/PO-token challenges. Without a JS runtime, YouTube downloads are blocked. yt-dlp requires deno >=2.3. Node (already in the toolbox, >=22) also works but is not default - opt in per-call/config with `--js-runtimes node`.

tools.name: tshark
tools.notes: CLI packet analysis (Wireshark backend); GUI at wireshark.exe

tools.name: etl2pcapng
tools.notes: convert pktmon/netsh-trace .etl captures to .pcapng for tshark/Wireshark (driver-free capture path)

tools.name: frida
tools.notes: dynamic instrumentation toolkit (toolbox venv)

tools.name: markdownlint-cli
tools.notes: markdown linter; run 'markdownlint **/*.md' to lint docs

tools.name: jupyterlab
tools.notes: Jupyter notebook server (toolbox venv); launch with 'jupyter-lab'

tools.name: sqlite-utils
tools.notes: SQLite CLI automation: insert, query, transform, export

tools.name: csvkit
tools.notes: CSV utilities: csvlook, csvcut, csvstat, csvjoin, in2csv, sql2csv

tools.name: pytoshop
tools.notes: write layered Photoshop .psd files from Python (import-only; no CLI)

tools.name: ollama
tools.notes: local LLM runtime; per-user background service at 127.0.0.1:11434 (OpenAI-compatible). Installed by scripts/install-llm.ps1, not the default groups.

toolbox_layers.name: native-cli
toolbox_layers.notes: native CLI tools: ffmpeg, pandoc, tesseract, rg, fd, jq, node, ...

llm.$comment: Optional local-LLM stack, provisioned by scripts/install-llm.ps1 (opt-in, not a default group). Ollama is the default runtime; llama.cpp is an opt-in alternative (see BACKLOG). Model pulls are VRAM-tiered so an 8 GB box does not waste disk on models it cannot run.

reranker.name: bge-reranker-base
reranker.notes: cross-encoder reranker run via the toolbox onnxruntime (not Ollama)

side_effects.$comment: Inventory of everything the toolbox mutates, so the uninstaller can reverse it. Paths under path_entries_relative are relative to the toolbox root (CODEX_TOOLBOX or %LOCALAPPDATA%\DevToolbox).
